title: The repository as the source of truth and the approval flow

videos.script: If the cluster does whatever the repository says, then whoever can write to the repository runs production. {{keys}} This lesson is about guarding that. You start a Git server of your own, called Gitea, in a container beside the cluster, and move lesson 1's history onto it. {{gitea}} Then you protect the main branch. Nobody pushes to it directly, not even an administrator. A change arrives as a pull request, and somebody other than its author approves it. {{rule}} You play both people. Ana proposes, Bruno reviews. Bruno reads two diffs: what changed in Git, and what would change in the cluster. {{review}} A small script plays the part of CI. It checks every proposed commit against the Kubernetes schemas, and the merge waits for it. {{checks}} And then you merge a change that is valid and wrong. The check passes, the cluster cannot run it, and the way back is another pull request. {{revert}}
